item.title: Cabinet to scrap welfare cuts in revised budget deal – RTL
item.description:
Cabinet to scrap welfare cuts in revised budget deal – RTL

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch government has scrapped most of its planned cuts to social security as it tries to attract opposition support for next year’s budget, RTL Nieuws has reported.

The cabinet will also delay raising the excess charge for health insurance by a year and invest €1.5 billion in mitigating the impact of inflation, particularly rising energy prices, on spending power.

The deal was the outcome of protracted negotiations between the three coalition partners, D66, VVD, and CDA, which ran through the weekend and most of Monday as the party leaders stretched the deadline to send the draft budget to the Council of State.

RTL Nieuws said it had seen leaked details of the budget proposals, which will not be formally announced for another two weeks when finance minister Eelco Heinen presents it to parliament.

The U-turn on welfare spending is a blow for the right-wing VVD, which had earlier said it would not compromise on the €6.5 billion worth of cuts to incapacity benefit, unemployment payments and substitute pay for new mothers on maternity leave.

Another plan in the coalition agreement to save €2.8 billion by increasing the retirement age in step with life expectancy, rather than by eight months for every extra year, has also been cancelled, as announced earlier by social security minister Hans Vijlbrief.

Heinen and prime minister Rob Jetten had spent the last two weeks trying to do a deal with opposition parties in advance to get their support for the budget, as the coalition is 10 seats short of a majority in the lower house and 16 seats short in the Senate.

But those talks ended without agreement as the three coalition parties struggled to agree among themselves about what concessions they should make to opposition groups on the left and right. Ministers will now have to find the votes when the budget plans go through parliament during the autumn.

Jetten’s D66 party and the Christian Democrats (CDA) reportedly wanted to scale back welfare cuts to appeal to the largest opposition party, the left-wing Progressief Nederland (Pro), while the VVD preferred a package that addressed the demands of right-wing parties such as JA21, with more tax cuts and less welfare spending.

item.title: Far-right TV show editor Niemöller leaves after Hitler remarks
item.description:
Far-right TV show editor Niemöller leaves after Hitler remarks

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Joost Niemöller is stepping down as editor-in-chief of far-right broadcaster Ongehoord Nederland (ON), weeks after he said on air that Adolf Hitler had put certain things “very well”.

The broadcaster said the immediate reason was a “difference of view about the editorial direction and recent programming”, according to director-general Peter Vlemmix. Its statement, reported by NOS, runs to two sentences and does not mention the item that set off weeks of criticism.

In the late-July broadcast, Niemöller said there were “certain things of Hitler’s” he agreed with, aside from the Nazi leader’s antisemitism.

Co-presenter Raisa Blommestijn also backed a statement, put to the pair after a clip of a Hitler speech referring to Jewish people, that a cosmopolitan elite was inherently hostile to ordinary people. Both said they did not share all of Hitler’s ideology.

Media minister Rianne Letschert called the broadcast “terrible, distasteful, hurtful and unnecessary”, and the ombudsman for the public broadcasters logged dozens of complaints. The cabinet is examining whether ON can be forced out of the public broadcasting system, and Letschert has said a decision will come “very soon”.

Ongehoord Nederland joined the public broadcasting system in 2022 and has been reprimanded and sanctioned several times for breaching journalistic rules. Niemöller became editor-in-chief about 18 months ago.

item.title: Three Dutch nationals remain missing after deadly Nepal floods
item.description:
Three Dutch nationals remain missing after deadly Nepal floods

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Rescue workers in Nepal are still trying to trace three Dutch nationals among more than 4,000 people reported missing since the devastating floods that swept through the border region with Tibet last week.

They include two tourists, 29-year-old Christiaan Berghuis from Nijkerk and 51-year-old Maaike Moolhuijsen from Haarlem, who were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, a sacred Tibetan mountain, when the disaster struck.

Their names were confirmed by the family support organisation Names de Familie. The third missing person is a Dutch woman who emigrated to Nepal, the foreign affairs ministry said.

The two visitors were part of a group of 80 people who were travelling from Kathmandu to Mount Kailash when a glacier in the Himalaya collapsed on Wednesday morning, causing the Bhote Koshi river to burst its banks and flood a large area with water and mud.

A spokesman for the Isha Foundation, which organised the trip, told RTL Nieuws the immigration office where the travellers were waiting at the time appeared to have been inundated.

Death toll passes 1,000

“At the moment nothing is known about the conditions of the people who were in the immigration office,” the spokesman said. “We are in constant contact with their families and are supporting them in every way possible.

“The last contact we had with our volunteer who was in charge of the group was around nine minutes before the flood happened.”

The Isha foundation was set up in 1992 by Jaggi Vasudev, an Indian yoga teacher better known by the name of Sandhguru.

A spokesman for the foreign affairs ministry said: “Their families in the Netherlands have been unable to contact them. The fear is that they were in the affected area at the moment of the flood.”

The death toll from the floods passed 1,000 on Tuesday as rescue workers continued to pull bodies from the water further downstream.

Altogether nearly 4,000 people are still unaccounted for in Nepal, as well as 546 in Tibet. They include around 900 hydropower workers who have been trapped in flooded tunnels for nearly a week.

item.title: Amsterdam taxi drivers launch app to rival Uber
item.description:
Amsterdam taxi drivers launch app to rival Uber

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A group of Amsterdam taxi drivers has launched a rival booking app to try and loosen Uber’s grip on the city’s cab market, amid long-running disputes over employee status, wages and workers’ rights. The founders claim nearly 1,300 drivers have already signed up.

The app, NLCabs, was set up by driver Mostapha Ahidar and co-founder Ivo van Leeuwen, who told Het Parool they were tired of watching a US monopoly control the terms of their trade. It works the same as Uber: passengers order a ride through the app and nearby drivers pick them up.

The difference, the founders say, is the cut. NLCabs takes a 3% commission from drivers, which Ahidar said was only what the platform needs to keep running. Uber’s commission is variable and can rise beyond half the fare, according to the drivers, though the company does not publish its rates.

“We are treated like children by Uber,” one driver told the paper. “We have absolutely no room for negotiation.”

Years of friction
The launch comes after years of conflict between Uber and Dutch drivers, much of which has gone through courts and regulators.

In August, the data protection authority (AP) fined Uber €825 million for deactivating drivers’ accounts through automated systems, without proper human review or explanation – the second-largest penalty ever issued under EU privacy law. Uber is appealing and has called the fine disproportionate.

That followed a €290 million fine in 2024 for sending drivers’ data to the US, a record at the time. Both cases originally stemmed from complaints by French drivers.

Employee or entrepreneur
In January, an Amsterdam appeal court ruled that Uber drivers cannot all be treated as employees, overturning a 2021 judgment that had put them on the payroll. The FNV trade union, which launched the case, said it was weighing a Supreme Court appeal.

Many drivers work almost exclusively through Uber and have little way of finding fares without it.

NLCabs is live but has only a few hundred downloads on Google Play, and the founders said they know shifting a habit as ingrained as opening Uber will be hard. They plan to expand across the Netherlands.

item.title: Groningen University launches Frisian language degree
item.description:
Groningen University launches Frisian language degree

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Groningen University has launched a bachelor’s degree programme in the Frisian language, the first standalone course in the country’s second official language for 15 years.

Three students began the course this week, which covers linguistics, history and Frisian culture. Frisian was taught as a degree in its own right until 2012, when it was absorbed into a broader programme on Europe’s minority languages, Minorities & Multilingualism.

That programme drew too few students to survive and the university said it would phase it out from the 2025/26 academic year, leaving the academic study of Frisian at risk of vanishing altogether.

A rescue from The Hague
The course was saved after the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) recommended, in a report on the future of Frisian studies, that the state pay for a dedicated bachelor. The government agreed to put in €340,000 a year, with further provincial money.

For legal reasons the new degree sits as a Frisian track within the university’s Dutch Languages and Cultures programme, though the focus is now entirely on Frisian.

Professor of Frisian Arjen Versloot said he was happy with the intake, even though a course usually needs around 20 students to break even. “There are often only five students in French and German too, so as a small language we can’t complain,” he told regional broadcaster Omrop Fryslân.

Teachers in demand
The degree is also meant to supply qualified teachers. Since August, schools in Friesland have been required to use more Frisian in the classroom under new curriculum rules, and Versloot expects strong demand for teachers able to deliver it at the highest level.

Frisian is spoken by around 470,000 people in Friesland and is the closest living relative of English.

Reading and writing proficiency in Frisian has risen sharply over the past two decades, despite fewer people speaking the language at home, according to a recent survey.

Around 58% of residents in Friesland now say they can read Frisian well or very well, up from 46% in 2007. Self-reported writing proficiency nearly doubled over the same period, from 9.6% to 18.9%.

item.title: Man cleared of plotting to kidnap princesses Amalia and Alexia
item.description:
Man cleared of plotting to kidnap princesses Amalia and Alexia

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A man has been cleared of plotting to kidnap princesses Amalia and Alexia, the eldest daughters of king Willem-Alexander and queen Máxima, after a court ruled he was suffering from a psychosis at the time.

Anne Romke van der H., 33, believed he was in a relationship with Amalia, 22, and fantasised about marrying her before living in the wilds in Poland with her and her 21-year-old sister.

He bought items from a hardware store designed to use as a survival kit, including knives, cooking equipment and two hatchets, one of which he inscribed with Alexia’s name.

The prosecution service said he intended to abduct or attack the two princesses if they were unwilling to go along with his plans.

But a court in The Hague ruled there was no evidence that van der H., from Groningen, was preparing an actual attack on Amalia and Alexia or intended to threaten them.

A psychiatric assessment found he was schizophrenic and had become obsessed with the royal family, particularly the two princesses.

He was found guilty of insulting six police officers and smashing a window, but the court did not impose a fine or punishment because he was in psychosis at the time.

The court said the offences were not severe enough to justify a compulsory treatment regime (tbs), but Van der H. told the judges at an earlier hearing that he was willing to undergo voluntary treatment.

item.title: Housing minister announces sites for 30,000 new homes by 2035
item.description:
Housing minister announces sites for 30,000 new homes by 2035

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Housing minister Eleanor Boekholt-O’Sullivan has identified five new sites around the country to build 30,000 new homes by 2035.

The five urban locations in Friesland, Noord-Holland, Zuid-Holland and Limburg have been designated National Large-Scale Housing Locations (NGWs) as part of the cabinet’s plans to build 400,000 houses in the next 10 years.

Between 5,000 and 6,000 homes are planned at four of the sites in Haarlem, Deventer, Weert and Leeuwarden, while 8,000 houses are due to be built in Maastricht. All the sites apart from Haarlem are close to main railway stations.

The sites are the first to be identified by the current government under the NGW scheme, a €5 billion fund first announced in 2023 to speed up development in urban areas and relieve the pressure on housing.

It takes the total number of NGW areas to 26. However, last month plans to develop four sites nominated by the previous housing minister, Mona Keijzer, had to be put on hold because there was no money to build road and railway connections.

Boekholt-O’Sullivan said in a letter to parliament that the locations had been chosen because they could be easily connected to services such as water and electricity, allowing the areas to be developed quickly.

“In choosing these five new NGW locations we explicitly looked at locations where no extra measures are needed for availability to realise these homes,” she said. “That means we can use our joint efforts to realise new neighbourhoods at speed.”

item.title: VVD MP quits lobby group board over conflict of interest claims
item.description:
VVD MP quits lobby group board over conflict of interest claims

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

VVD MP Renate den Hollander has resigned from the management board of a vets’ lobby group after facing questions about her role as the party’s spokesman on animal welfare.

NOS reported that some of Den Hollander’s comments in parliament were almost identical to statements made by the BPW, an organisation representing owners of veterinary practices.

Den Hollander, 49, spent 22 as a vet and ran her own practice in Drenthe before being elected to parliament for the first time last November. She was a member of the BPW before becoming an MP, but only joined the board this year.

NOS reported that her response to a report by the consumer markets watchdog ACM that criticised high vets’ bills and unnecessary procedures was strikingly similar to the BPW’s official line.

Den Hollander said the VVD did not share all the ACM’s criticisms, stressed the need for veterinary staff to be paid properly and suggested alternative solutions to deal with rising costs such as encouraging people to take out more insurance.

Identical language

Although she was not a member of the board at the time, Den Hollander used almost identical language to the BPW in its response, such as comparing vets to other business owners such as bakers and garage owners.

A month later she was taken on as a member of the management board with an allowance of €1,000 a year.

In a written reply to NOS, she said she was stepping down from the board with immediate effect after the national broadcaster compared her speech with the BPW’s statement.

“The similarities to a contribution I later made as an MP, which you have rightly asked questions about. have made me realise that my membership of the management board of the BPW could lead in future to (the appearance of) a conflict of interests,” she said.

item.title: Cabinet agrees 11th-hour budget deal without opposition support
item.description:
Cabinet agrees 11th-hour budget deal without opposition support

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The coalition parties D66, CDA and VVD have agreed a draft budget package after a marathon weekend of “tough” and “intensive” talks.

Finance minister Eelco Heinen said the negotiations had produced a “budget for 10 parties”, but the minority government was unable to secure the approval of opposition parties before the plans are presented to parliament on September 15.

Instead the three coalition partners had to resolve their own differences on issues such as welfare cuts, changes to the system for taxing wealth and assets and the higher excess charge on health insurance.

Heinen and prime minister Rob Jetten did not disclose what concessions had been made during the negotiations, but party leaders said they had produced a balanced package designed to appeal to both left and right.

Jetten acknowledged the negotiations had been “tough” at times. “Occasionally there was a bit of friction, but that gave us a more polished budget,” he said.

Dilan Yesilgöz, leader of the VVD, said in a post on X that the cabinet had produced a budget “that can take the Netherlands forward”, while emphasising her party’s campaign points.

“The VVD wil always stand for lower taxes, room for economic growth and a government that spends less,” she said. Earlier Yesilgöz described the negotiations as “long and intensive”.

We zijn eruit. Na lange en intensieve onderhandelingen ligt er een begroting waarmee Nederland vooruit kan. De VVD staat daarbij altijd voor lagere lasten, ruimte voor economische groei en een overheid die minder uitgeeft.

In een kabinet betekent verantwoordelijkheid nemen ook:…

— Dilan Yesilgöz – Zegerius (@DilanYesilgoz) August 31, 2026

Henri Bontenbal, leader of the CDA, said: “My aim was to come up with a good offer to the opposition. I think we’ve managed that.”

Minority government

Jetten and Heinen spent two weeks talking to opposition party leaders behind closed doors to try to secure their support for the budget before the draft package was sent to the Council of State.

But those negotiations broke down at the end of last week without producing a formal deal, meaning the cabinet will have to find the votes as the bills pass through parliament in the autumn.

The government is 10 seats short of a majority in the Lower House and 16 short in the smaller Senate, where it needs the support of at least two opposition parties.

The original deadline of last Friday was extended over the weekend and into an extra cabinet meeting on Monday afternoon as the divisions within the coalition became harder to reconcile.

The centre parties, D66 and CDA, wanted to scrap some of the proposed €6.5 billion budget cuts planned for the next four years to appeal to Progressief Nederland (PRO), the largest opposition party, which was previously the left-wing alliance of Labour (PvdA) and GroenLinks.

“Problems delayed”

But the VVD favoured a different package of measures designed to bring on board right-wing parties such as JA21 and the SGP, who wanted to see tax cuts instead.

The parties also had different visions of how to reform the “box 3” income tax module, which covers assets and savings, with the VVD arguing for a more generous deal for investors.

The VVD justice minister, David van Weel, said “nobody is proud of this process, nobody is happy with it” ahead of Monday’s meeting, where the draft budget was agreed.

Pro leader Jesse Klaver said he feared that the coalition parties had “not made choices” and “the problems have been delayed” until after the budget is presented on September 15.

item.title: Police arrest 34 after deadly shooting in Gelderland village
item.description:
Police arrest 34 after deadly shooting in Gelderland village

September 1, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

One man has died and two police officers were injured in a suspected gang-related shooting in Overasselt, a village in Gelderland, in the early hours of Tuesday. Police have arrested 34 people and say the attack stemmed from a “long-running conflict.”

At an afternoon press conference, the deputy head of the police’s eastern Netherlands unit, Jolanda Aalbers, said the man who died was 51 and came from the nearby town of Wijchen. He is reported to have been a security guard hired to protect the property that was targeted.

The two officers, who were first on the scene, were given first aid by colleagues “while they were under fire,” Aalbers said. Both are now out of danger. Weapons and vehicles have been seized, and the 34 people arrested include French, Belgian, Algerian and Dutch nationals, according to the public prosecution department.

They are being questioned on suspicion of involvement in murder, manslaughter and attempted manslaughter.

Heumen mayor Joerie Minses urged residents of Overasselt and neighbouring Nederasselt to follow police instructions and stay indoors where possible. Justice minister David van Weel described the events as “horrific”.

Unverified images shared by the Telegraaf show a group of at least 30 masked men – some carrying what appear to be automatic rifles – outside a property. NOS, which reviewed later security footage, said it appeared to show an execution: an armed group approaches a parked car with its interior light on, and one person opens fire before most of the group runs off.

Officers were first called to the Ewijkseweg in the village at around 4am, and a specialist ambulance team whose staff wear bulletproof vests was sent from Amsterdam after reports of automatic gunfire, according to NOS. The team is deployed only in cases of extreme violence.

Police and prosecutors declined to confirm reports linking the attack to fugitive drug lord Jos Leijdekkers, known as Bolle Jos, or to a missing cocaine shipment. Het Parool, citing sources, reported that the dispute concerned a consignment of more than 800 kilos of cocaine seized on August 29 at the Spanish-French border, part of which may have reached the Netherlands.

Prosecutors said the property was also shot at last year. According to police, a man in his twenties from Amsterdam fired 25 rounds from a Kalashnikov in July 2025 and left behind photographs as a warning. He said he had been promised €2,500 but never revealed who paid him, and was sentenced to a year in juvenile detention; his driver was given 10 months.

One of the residents of the property was this year sentenced to four years in prison for a “coordinating role” in an MDMA lab in the Gelderland village of Angeren, which was shut down in 2021. He denies involvement.

A large-scale police operation continued through the day in and around Overasselt, with helicopters, dogs and arrest teams searching the area. Several of those detained were found hiding in bushes, and a reporter from broadcaster Powned said three “young boys,” some barefoot, were caught about 2km from the village after a passer-by alerted police.

Further arrests were made on the A73 and A76 motorways, which police confirmed are connected to the investigation. Armed officers also searched a train at Nijmegen station; three men who asked for directions in French at a nearby ROC vocational college were later detained, though police have not confirmed a link to Overasselt.
